Instant Pot green chili

25 minutes 6 servings Freezer-friendly

This is the green chili I make on weeknights when the first cold snap hits. Broiling the vegetables before pressure cooking is the only extra step, and it is the difference between flat and deeply flavored. Serve with warm tortillas and a squeeze of lime.

Ingredients

  • 1.5 lbs pork shoulder, cubed
  • 1 lb tomatillos, husked and halved
  • 2 poblano peppers
  • 1 white onion, quartered
  • 3 cloves garlic
  • 2 cans white beans, drained
  • 4 cups chicken stock

Method

  1. Broil tomatillos, poblanos, onion, and garlic until charred, about 8 minutes. Blend with a cup of stock until smooth.
  2. Turn the Instant Pot to sauté, brown the pork on all sides, then add the purée, beans, and remaining stock.
  3. Pressure cook 15 minutes with natural release. Shred larger pork chunks against the side of the pot and season to taste.

Notes and swaps

For extra heat leave one poblano's seeds in. Chicken thighs work in place of pork; reduce pressure cook time to 10 minutes. The chili thickens overnight and freezes for three months.

To make it in a slow cooker, broil and blend the vegetables the night before, then combine everything on low for eight hours. You will lose the fond from the sauté step, so add a teaspoon of tomato paste for depth.

Serving suggestions

  • Warm flour tortillas and a squeeze of lime
  • Cotija cheese and sliced radishes
  • Avocado crema: blend one avocado with lime juice and salt

Storage

Refrigerate for up to five days; the flavor improves on day two. Freeze in flat quart bags for up to three months and thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating gently on the stovetop.
